definition: Coming after something else in time; following or succeeding in a chronological order.
definition_zh: 隨後的；後來的；接續的

mnemonic.story_en: In a SUB (close after) sequence, the SEQUI (following) events will show the SUBSEQUENT impact of the decision.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在緊接而來的序列中，跟隨（SEQUI）在後（SUB）的事件將揭示該決定的「隨後（SUBSEQUENT）」影響。
mnemonic.root_memory: SUB = under, close after; connect this root idea with subsequent.

example: The initial study was flawed, but subsequent research confirmed the medication's effectiveness.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 subsequent 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: following is related, but subsequent has its own usage pattern and context.
succeeding may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with subsequent.

usage_note: subsequent is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To provide evidence to support or prove the truth of a claim, theory, or allegation.
definition_zh: 證實；證明...有根據

mnemonic.story_en: You must find solid substance under the claim so that it can STAnd firmly and SUBSTANTIATE your argument in court.
mnemonic.story_zh: 你必須在指控下方找到實質證據，使其能夠穩固站（STAre）立，進而「證實（SUBSTANTIATE）」你在法庭上的論點。
mnemonic.root_memory: SUB = under; connect this root idea with substantiate.

example: The prosecutor failed to provide sufficient evidence to substantiate the charges against the suspect.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 substantiate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: corroborate is related, but substantiate has its own usage pattern and context.
verify may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with substantiate.

usage_note: substantiate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Existing or occurring at or on the surface; lacking depth, substance, or thoroughness.
definition_zh: 表面的；膚淺的；草率的

mnemonic.story_en: He only looked at the SUPER (above) FACIES (face) of the problem, making a very SUPERFICIAL analysis.
mnemonic.story_zh: 他只看問題之（SUPER）上的表面（FACIES），做出了非常「膚淺的（SUPERFICIAL）」分析。
mnemonic.root_memory: SUPER = above, over; connect this root idea with superficial.

example: The committee made a superficial review of the proposal without analyzing its long-term financial risks.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 superficial 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: shallow is related, but superficial has its own usage pattern and context.
surface-level may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with superficial.

usage_note: superficial is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To take the place of a person or thing previously in authority or use; to replace or supplant.
definition_zh: 取代；替代；廢棄（因新事物出現）

mnemonic.story_en: The new digital technology will SUPER (above) SEDE (sit) the old analog systems completely.
mnemonic.story_zh: 新數位技術將坐（SEDE）在舊類比系統之（SUPER）上，完全「取代（SUPERSEDE）」它。
mnemonic.root_memory: SUPER = above, over; connect this root idea with supersede.

example: Most of these old regulations have been superseded by the new environmental protection law.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 supersede 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: replace is related, but supersede has its own usage pattern and context.
supplant may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with supersede.

usage_note: supersede is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Perceptible by touch; clear and definite; real rather than imaginary.
definition_zh: 有形的；實質的；可觸摸到的；明確的

mnemonic.story_en: Without TANGible assets that you can TANG (touch), the bank will not approve your business loan.
mnemonic.story_zh: 如果沒有可以用手觸（TANG）摸到的「有形（TANGIBLE）」資產，銀行不會批准你的商業貸款。
mnemonic.root_memory: TANG / TANGERE = to touch; connect this root idea with tangible.

example: The police are looking for tangible evidence, such as fingerprints or DNA, rather than mere speculation.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 tangible 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: concrete is related, but tangible has its own usage pattern and context.
palpable may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with tangible.

usage_note: tangible is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Not certain or fixed; done without confidence; hesitant or provisional.
definition_zh: 暫定的；嘗試性的；猶豫不決的

mnemonic.story_en: They made a TENTative schedule to TENT (try) out the new system before making it permanent.
mnemonic.story_zh: 他們制定了一個「暫定的（TENTATIVE）」時程表來嘗（TENT）試新系統，之後才會定案。
mnemonic.root_memory: TENT / TEMPTARE = to feel, try, test; connect this root idea with tentative.

example: We have reached a tentative agreement, but it still needs to be ratified by the board of directors.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 tentative 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: provisional is related, but tentative has its own usage pattern and context.
conditional may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with tentative.

usage_note: tentative is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Lasting only for a short time; impermanent or fleeting.
definition_zh: 短暫的；轉瞬即逝的；過客的

mnemonic.story_en: The storm was TRANsient, quickly TRANS (crossing) over the city and leaving as fast as it arrived.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這場暴風雨是「短暫的（TRANSIENT）」，迅速穿（TRANS）過城市，來得快去得也快。
mnemonic.root_memory: TRANS = across, through; connect this root idea with transient.

example: The economic boom turned out to be transient, followed quickly by a severe recession.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 transient 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: fleeting is related, but transient has its own usage pattern and context.
ephemeral may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with transient.

usage_note: transient is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Never done or known before; without any previous example or parallel case.
definition_zh: 史無前例的；空前的

mnemonic.story_en: The country experienced UNprecedented growth, which had never PRE-CEDEd (gone before) it in history.
mnemonic.story_zh: 該國經歷了「史無前例的（UNPRECEDENTED）」增長，這在歷史上從未有走在前面（PRE-CEDE）的先例。
mnemonic.root_memory: UN- = not; connect this root idea with unprecedented.

example: The government took the unprecedented step of closing all national borders to contain the virus.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 unprecedented 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: unparalleled is related, but unprecedented has its own usage pattern and context.
exceptional may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with unprecedented.

usage_note: unprecedented is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Showing strong feeling; forceful, passionate, or intense in expression or emotion.
definition_zh: 強烈的；猛烈的；熱情的；（常指激動地）強烈反對的

mnemonic.story_en: Driven by a powerful VEHEment impulse, his MENS (mind) exploded into a VEHEMENT denial of the charges.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在強烈情緒的載（VEHE）運下，他的心智（MENS）爆發出對指控的「強烈（VEHEMENT）」否認。
mnemonic.root_memory: VEHERE = to carry, convey; connect this root idea with vehement.

example: Despite vehement opposition from local residents, the city council approved the construction of the landfill.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 vehement 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: passionate is related, but vehement has its own usage pattern and context.
forceful may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with vehement.

usage_note: vehement is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Susceptible to physical or emotional attack or harm; unprotected and easily damaged.
definition_zh: 易受傷的；脆弱的；易受攻擊的

mnemonic.story_en: Without a shield, the soldier's chest was left VULNERable to a fatal VULNER (wound).
mnemonic.story_zh: 沒有盾牌保護，士兵的胸膛很容易受傷（VULNER），處於「易受攻擊的（VULNERABLE）」狀態。
mnemonic.root_memory: VULNERARE / VULNUS = to wound, injury; connect this root idea with vulnerable.

example: Older people and young children are particularly vulnerable to influenza during the winter months.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 vulnerable 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: susceptible is related, but vulnerable has its own usage pattern and context.
exposed may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with vulnerable.

usage_note: vulnerable is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Feeling or showing caution about possible dangers or problems; alert and watchful.
definition_zh: 謹慎的；警惕的；唯恐的

mnemonic.story_en: Be aWARE and stay WARY of strangers who offer you investments that sound too good to be true.
mnemonic.story_zh: 隨時保持意識（aWARE），對那些聽起來好得令人難以置信的投資項目保持「警惕（WARY）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: WAR / WAER = watchful, guarded; connect this root idea with wary.

example: Investors are increasingly wary of putting money into high-risk startups during an economic downturn.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 wary 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: cautious is related, but wary has its own usage pattern and context.
circumspect vigilant may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with wary.

usage_note: wary is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A departure from what is normal, usual, or expected, typically one that is unwelcome.
definition_zh: 異常；偏差；偏離常軌（通常指不良的）

mnemonic.story_en: The player's violent outburst was a temporary ABERRATION from his AB- (away) normal calm behavior, caused by ERRARE (straying) from his training.
mnemonic.story_zh: 該球員的暴力爆發只是暫時遠離（AB）冷靜軌道、走入迷途（ERRARE）的「異常（ABERRATION）」行為。
mnemonic.root_memory: AB- = away from; connect this root idea with aberration.

example: The sudden drop in sales was a temporary aberration caused by a computer glitch rather than a market trend.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 aberration 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: anomaly is related, but aberration has its own usage pattern and context.
deviation may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with aberration.

usage_note: aberration is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To accept something reluctantly but without protest; to comply silently.
definition_zh: 默許；勉強同意；默從

mnemonic.story_en: The manager decided to ACQUIESCE to the demands, remaining QUIET (quiescere) instead of arguing.
mnemonic.story_zh: 經理決定「默許（ACQUIESCE）」這些要求，保持安靜（QUIESCERE）而不再爭辯。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = to, toward; connect this root idea with acquiesce.

example: The director chose to acquiesce to the board's decision rather than risking his position by protesting.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 acquiesce 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: comply is related, but acquiesce has its own usage pattern and context.
concede may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with acquiesce.

usage_note: acquiesce is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Experienced to a severe or intense degree; having or showing a perceptive understanding or insight; (of an angle) less than 90°.
definition_zh: 嚴重的；敏銳的；急性的（疾病）；銳角的

mnemonic.story_en: The patient felt an ACUTE pain that was as sharp as an ACUs (needle) piercing the skin.
mnemonic.story_zh: 病患感受到「劇烈的（ACUTE）」疼痛，就像針（ACUs）尖刺入皮膚一樣銳利。
mnemonic.root_memory: ACUS / ACUERE = needle, to sharpen; connect this root idea with acute.

example: The company is facing an acute shortage of skilled software engineers, threatening its project deadlines.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 acute 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: severe is related, but acute has its own usage pattern and context.
intense may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with acute.

usage_note: acute is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To stick fast to a surface or substance; to believe in and follow the practices or rules of something.
definition_zh: 黏附；堅持；遵守（規則或信念）

mnemonic.story_en: Glue makes the poster ADHERE to the wall, just as professional athletes must ADHERE to strict rules.
mnemonic.story_zh: 膠水讓海報黏（HAERE）在牆壁上，就像職業運動員必須「遵守（ADHERE）」嚴格的規章一樣。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = to, toward; connect this root idea with adhere.

example: All laboratory personnel must strictly adhere to safety protocols to prevent chemical contamination.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 adhere 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: stick is related, but adhere has its own usage pattern and context.
cling may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with adhere.

usage_note: adhere is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Preventing success or development; harmful, unfavorable, or hostile.
definition_zh: 不利的；有害的；反向的

mnemonic.story_en: When the wind shifts and turns ADVERSEly against your ship, you face ADVERSE weather conditions.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當風向改變、轉（VERTERE）向與你的船作對時，你就面臨了「不利的（ADVERSE）」天氣條件。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = toward; connect this root idea with adverse.

example: The pharmaceutical company reported that the new drug has no adverse side effects on patients.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 adverse 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: unfavorable is related, but adverse has its own usage pattern and context.
disadvantageous may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with adverse.

usage_note: adverse is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To officially end a law, system, institution, or practice, especially because it is considered unfair or unnecessary.
definition_zh: 廢除；取消；終止

roots.meaning: to destroy, cause to die out

mnemonic.root_memory: ABOLERE = cause to die out; abolish means making an old rule disappear.
mnemonic.story_en: Reformers ABOLISHED the unfair law so it would finally die out of public life.
mnemonic.story_zh: 改革者「廢除（ABOLISH）」不公平的法律，讓它從公共生活中消失。

example: The government voted to abolish the outdated tax after years of public criticism.
example_zh: 多年公眾批評後，政府投票廢除這項過時稅制。

near_synonyms.difference: repeal is specifically to cancel a law; abolish can apply to laws, systems, or practices.
eliminate means remove; abolish stresses official or institutional ending.

usage_note: abolish is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: Concerning or characterized by an appreciation of beauty or good taste, especially in art.
definition_zh: 美學的；審美的；具有美感的

mnemonic.story_en: The modern building was designed with great AESTHETIC appeal, pleasing the visual senses of everyone.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這棟現代建築的設計具有極高的「美感（AESTHETIC）」，取悅了每個人的視覺感官。
mnemonic.root_memory: AISTHETIKOS = perceptive, of sense perception; connect this root idea with aesthetic.

example: The product's minimalist design emphasizes both functional utility and aesthetic appeal.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 aesthetic 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: artistic is related, but aesthetic has its own usage pattern and context.
beautiful may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with aesthetic.

usage_note: aesthetic is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To cause someone to feel isolated, estranged, or excluded from a group or society.
definition_zh: 疏遠；使孤立；轉讓（財產）

mnemonic.story_en: The politician's extreme comments managed to ALIENATE moderate voters, making them feel like ALIENs in the party.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這位政治人物的極端言論成功「疏遠了（ALIENATE）」溫和派選民，讓他們在黨內感覺像外星人（ALIEN）一樣格格不入。
mnemonic.root_memory: ALIUS / ALIENUS = other, another, foreign; connect this root idea with alienate.

example: His arrogant behavior tended to alienate his colleagues, leaving him isolated in the office.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 alienate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: estrange is related, but alienate has its own usage pattern and context.
isolate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with alienate.

usage_note: alienate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: The belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.
definition_zh: 利他主義；無私

mnemonic.story_en: Act with ALTRUISM by putting the needs of ALTER (others) before your own selfish desires.
mnemonic.story_zh: 展現「利他主義（ALTRUISM）」，就要把其他（ALTER）人的需求放在自己的自私欲望之前。
mnemonic.root_memory: ALTER = other; connect this root idea with altruism.

example: Many charities rely on the pure altruism of volunteers who dedicate their time without pay.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 altruism 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: unselfishness is related, but altruism has its own usage pattern and context.
philanthropy may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with altruism.

usage_note: altruism is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To formally free someone from blame, guilt, or responsibility for something.
definition_zh: 免除責任；宣告無罪；赦免

mnemonic.root_memory: AB + SOLV = loosen away; absolve releases someone from guilt.
mnemonic.story_en: The inquiry ABSOLVED the manager by loosening the blame attached to her name.
mnemonic.story_zh: 調查把責任從經理身上鬆開（SOLV），因此「免除（ABSOLVE）」她的責任。

example: The report did not absolve senior officials of responsibility for the failed project.
example_zh: 該報告並未免除高階官員對失敗專案的責任。

near_synonyms.difference: forgive is personal or moral; absolve is formal and often concerns responsibility.
excuse may overlook a fault; absolve declares someone free from blame.

usage_note: absolve is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: A comparison between two things, typically for the purpose of explanation or clarification.
definition_zh: 類比；比喻；相似物

mnemonic.story_en: The teacher drew an ANALOGY, comparing the human brain to a computer based on LOGOS (reason).
mnemonic.story_zh: 老師做了一個「類比（ANALOGY）」，根（ANA）據邏輯（LOGOS）將人類大腦比作電腦。
mnemonic.root_memory: ANA- = upon, according to; connect this root idea with analogy.

example: To explain how electricity flows in a wire, the professor used the analogy of water flowing through a pipe.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 analogy 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: comparison is related, but analogy has its own usage pattern and context.
metaphor may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with analogy.

usage_note: analogy is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To destroy utterly; to wipe out of existence; to defeat completely.
definition_zh: 殲滅；消滅；徹底擊敗

mnemonic.story_en: The atomic bomb can ANNIHILATE an entire city, turning all buildings into NIHIL (nothing).
mnemonic.story_zh: 原子彈能「徹底消滅（ANNIHILATE）」整座城市，將所有建築物化為虛無（NIHIL）。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = to, toward; connect this root idea with annihilate.

example: The heavy artillery fire managed to annihilate the enemy's defensive fortifications within hours.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 annihilate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: destroy is related, but annihilate has its own usage pattern and context.
obliterate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with annihilate.

usage_note: annihilate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.
definition_zh: 異常事物；反常現象；畸變

mnemonic.story_en: A snowfall in the desert is a weather ANOMALY, because it is AN (not) HOMALOS (regular) for that climate.
mnemonic.story_zh: 沙漠降雪是一種氣候「反常現象（ANOMALY）」，因為這對當地的氣候來說是不（AN）常規（HOMALOS）的。
mnemonic.root_memory: AN- = not, without; connect this root idea with anomaly.

example: Scientists discovered a genetic anomaly in the blood sample that could explain the patient's rare condition.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 anomaly 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: abnormality is related, but anomaly has its own usage pattern and context.
irregularity may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with anomaly.

usage_note: anomaly is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Showing or feeling no interest, enthusiasm, or concern; listless or indifferent.
definition_zh: 冷漠的；無動於衷的；缺乏興趣的

mnemonic.story_en: Many APATHETIC citizens remain APATHETIC about elections, staying A- (without) PATHOS (feeling) for politics.
mnemonic.story_zh: 許多「冷漠的（APATHETIC）」公民對選舉無動於衷，對政治抱持著沒（A）有感情（PATHOS）的態度。
mnemonic.root_memory: A- = without; connect this root idea with apathetic.

example: The youth are often accused of being apathetic toward local politics, resulting in low voter turnout.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 apathetic 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: indifferent is related, but apathetic has its own usage pattern and context.
unconcerned may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with apathetic.

usage_note: apathetic is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason, system, or law; (of power) autocratic or tyrannical.
definition_zh: 任意的；隨機的；武斷的；專制的

mnemonic.story_en: The dictator made an ARBITRARY decision, acting like a tyrannical ARBITER who ignores the written law.
mnemonic.story_zh: 獨裁者做了一個「武斷的（ARBITRARY）」決定，表現得像一個無視成文法律的專制仲裁者（ARBITER）。
mnemonic.root_memory: ARBITER = judge, witness; connect this root idea with arbitrary.

example: The selection of the winners seemed completely arbitrary, with no clear criteria provided by the judges.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 arbitrary 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: random is related, but arbitrary has its own usage pattern and context.
capricious may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with arbitrary.

usage_note: arbitrary is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Showing great care, attention, and persistent effort; diligent and hard-working.
definition_zh: 專心致志的；勤勉的；鍥而不捨的

mnemonic.story_en: The ASSIDUOUS student would SEDE (sit) at her desk for hours, working diligently on her research paper.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這位「勤勉的（ASSIDUOUS）」學生會連續幾個小時坐（SEDE）在書桌前，專心致志地寫著她的研究論文。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = to, near; connect this root idea with assiduous.

example: Through assiduous research and hours of interviews, the journalist finally uncovered the corporate scandal.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 assiduous 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: diligent is related, but assiduous has its own usage pattern and context.
industrious may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with assiduous.

usage_note: assiduous is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To make something greater, larger, or more intense by adding to it; to increase.
definition_zh: 增加；擴大；擴充；提高

mnemonic.story_en: He had to AUGMENT his income by taking a second job, AUG- (increasing) his total savings.
mnemonic.story_zh: 他不得不兼差第二份工作來「增加（AUGMENT）」收入，以擴大（AUGERE）他的總存款。
mnemonic.root_memory: AUGERE = to increase, make grow; connect this root idea with augment.

example: The military decided to augment its forces in the region due to rising political tensions.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 augment 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: increase is related, but augment has its own usage pattern and context.
enhance may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with augment.

usage_note: augment is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Severe or strict in manner, attitude, or appearance; having no comforts or luxuries; plain and unadorned.
definition_zh: 嚴厲的；簡樸的；苦行的；毫無裝飾的

mnemonic.story_en: The monk lived a very AUSTERE life in an AUSTERE room with nothing but a wooden bed.
mnemonic.story_zh: 僧侶在一間除了木床外別無他物的「簡樸（AUSTERE）」房間裡，過著非常苦（AUSTEROS）行簡樸的生活。
mnemonic.root_memory: AUSTEROS = bitter, harsh, dry; connect this root idea with austere.

example: During the economic crisis, the government introduced austere measures to reduce the national debt.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 austere 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: ascetic is related, but austere has its own usage pattern and context.
stark may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with austere.

usage_note: austere is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To deliberately avoid doing or consuming something; also to choose not to vote.
definition_zh: 戒絕；避免；投棄權票

mnemonic.root_memory: ABS + TAIN = hold away from; abstain means keeping yourself away from an action.
mnemonic.story_en: The senator ABSTAINED from the vote, holding herself away from both sides.
mnemonic.story_zh: 參議員讓自己遠離（ABS）表決雙方，因此「棄權（ABSTAIN）」。

example: Several board members abstained because they had financial ties to the applicant.
example_zh: 幾位董事因與申請者有財務關係而投棄權票。

near_synonyms.difference: refuse is active rejection; abstain is deliberate non-participation.
avoid is general; abstain often suggests discipline or formal voting.

usage_note: abstain is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: Well-meaning and kindly; serving a charitable rather than a profit-making purpose.
definition_zh: 仁慈的；慈善的；善意的

mnemonic.story_en: The BENEVOLENT king always wished BENE (well) for his people, showing great kindness.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這位「仁慈的（BENEVOLENT）」國王總是祝願（VELLE）他的子民過得好（BENE），展現了極大的善良。
mnemonic.root_memory: BENE = well, good; connect this root idea with benevolent.

example: The local orphanage was entirely funded by a benevolent billionaire who wished to remain anonymous.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 benevolent 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: kindly is related, but benevolent has its own usage pattern and context.
charitable may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with benevolent.

usage_note: benevolent is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behavior; fickle and unpredictable.
definition_zh: 變化無常的；任性的；善變的

mnemonic.story_en: The dictator's CAPRICIOUS moods changed as fast as a CAPRA (goat) leaping randomly in the mountains.
mnemonic.story_zh: 獨裁者「變化無常的（CAPRICIOUS）」情緒，就像在山中胡亂跳躍的山羊（CAPRA）一樣快。
mnemonic.root_memory: CAPRA = goat; connect this root idea with capricious.

example: The administration's capricious policy changes left local business owners confused and unable to plan ahead.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 capricious 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: fickle is related, but capricious has its own usage pattern and context.
unpredictable may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with capricious.

usage_note: capricious is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change; a person or thing that precipitates an event or change.
definition_zh: 催化劑；促成者；引發改變的人或事物

mnemonic.story_en: The assassination of the archduke acted as a CATALYST, thoroughly LYEIN (loosening) the fragile peace and starting World War I.
mnemonic.story_zh: 大公被刺殺事件充當了「催化劑（CATALYST）」，徹底解開（LYEIN）了脆弱的和平，引發了第一次世界大戰。
mnemonic.root_memory: KATA- = down, thoroughly; connect this root idea with catalyst.

example: The publication of the book served as a catalyst for the nationwide civil rights movement.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 catalyst 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: stimulus is related, but catalyst has its own usage pattern and context.
spark may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with catalyst.

usage_note: catalyst is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: (of an illness or problem) persisting for a long time or constantly recurring.
definition_zh: 慢性的（疾病）；長期的；根深蒂固的

mnemonic.story_en: He suffered from CHRONIC back pain, which haunted him for a long CHRONOS (time).
mnemonic.story_zh: 他患有「慢性的（CHRONIC）」背痛，這困擾了他很長的時間（CHRONOS）。
mnemonic.root_memory: CHRONOS = time; connect this root idea with chronic.

example: The country is suffering from chronic unemployment, which the government has failed to fix for a decade.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 chronic 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: persistent is related, but chronic has its own usage pattern and context.
long-standing may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with chronic.

usage_note: chronic is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Wary and unwilling to take risks; cautious and prudent before acting.
definition_zh: 謹慎的；考慮周密的；慎重的

mnemonic.story_en: A CIRCUMSPECT general will always CIRCUM (around) SPEC (look) at the terrain before ordering an attack.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一位「謹慎的（CIRCUMSPECT）」將軍在下令進攻前，總會向四周（CIRCUM）環顧觀察（SPECERE）地形。
mnemonic.root_memory: CIRCUM = around; connect this root idea with circumspect.

example: Officials were circumspect in their statements to the press, avoiding any mention of the ongoing investigation.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 circumspect 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: cautious is related, but circumspect has its own usage pattern and context.
prudent may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with circumspect.

usage_note: circumspect is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To make something happen faster or to increase in speed, rate, or progress.
definition_zh: 加速；促進；加快

mnemonic.root_memory: CELER = fast; accelerate means making movement or change faster.
mnemonic.story_en: New funding ACCELERATED the research, making progress move at a faster pace.
mnemonic.story_zh: 新資金讓研究變快（CELER），因此「加速（ACCELERATE）」進展。

example: Digital tools can accelerate data collection, but they do not guarantee better analysis.
example_zh: 數位工具可以加速資料蒐集，但不保證分析更好。

near_synonyms.difference: increase means become larger; accelerate specifically means become faster.
facilitate makes easier; accelerate makes faster.

usage_note: accelerate is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: Easy to reach, enter, use, understand, or obtain, especially for a wide range of people.
definition_zh: 可接近的；可使用的；容易理解的

mnemonic.root_memory: CESS = go; accessible means people can go toward or use something.
mnemonic.story_en: The city made the website ACCESSIBLE so every resident could reach public services online.
mnemonic.story_zh: 城市讓網站「可使用（ACCESSIBLE）」，使每位居民都能接近（CESS）公共服務。

example: The museum redesigned its entrance to make the building accessible to wheelchair users.
example_zh: 博物館重新設計入口，讓輪椅使用者也能進入。

near_synonyms.difference: convenient means easy to use; accessible also stresses reach, inclusion, or understandability.
understandable concerns meaning; accessible can concern physical or digital access.

usage_note: accessible is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: Showing smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements, often while remaining unaware of upcoming dangers.
definition_zh: 自滿的；沾沾自喜的；盲目樂觀的

mnemonic.story_en: The champion became COMPLACENT, so thoroughly PLEASed (placere) with his past wins that he stopped training hard.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這位冠軍變得「自滿（COMPLACENT）」，對自己過去的勝利感到太過高興（PLACERE），以至於停止了刻苦訓練。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = intensive prefix; connect this root idea with complacent.

example: We cannot afford to become complacent about market competition, as rival startups are launching new products every month.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 complacent 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: smug is related, but complacent has its own usage pattern and context.
self-satisfied may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with complacent.

usage_note: complacent is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To provide space, support, or adjustment for someone or something; also to adapt to a need or condition.
definition_zh: 容納；提供住宿；配合；調整以適應

mnemonic.root_memory: COMMODUS = suitable; accommodate means making conditions suitable for someone.
mnemonic.story_en: The school ACCOMMODATED students by adjusting the schedule to fit their needs.
mnemonic.story_zh: 學校調整課表使其合適（COMMODUS），以「配合（ACCOMMODATE）」學生需求。

example: The software can accommodate different screen sizes without losing key functions.
example_zh: 這套軟體可以適應不同螢幕尺寸而不失去主要功能。

near_synonyms.difference: include means contain as part; accommodate means make room or adjustment.
tolerate means allow despite dislike; accommodate is more supportive.

usage_note: accommodate is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: The quality of being correct, exact, and free from error, especially in measurement, reporting, or judgment.
definition_zh: 準確性；精確度；正確性

mnemonic.root_memory: CURA = care; accuracy comes from careful attention to correctness.
mnemonic.story_en: The scientist checked every number with care to protect the ACCURACY of the results.
mnemonic.story_zh: 科學家仔細（CURA）檢查每個數字，以確保結果的「準確性（ACCURACY）」。

example: The accuracy of the survey depends on both sample size and question design.
example_zh: 調查的準確性取決於樣本數與問題設計。

near_synonyms.difference: precision stresses fine detail; accuracy stresses closeness to the truth or correct value.
reliability means consistency; accuracy means correctness.

usage_note: accuracy is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: To accept and allow (behavior that is considered morally wrong or offensive) to continue; to overlook or forgive.
definition_zh: 縱容；寬恕；默許（壞事）

mnemonic.story_en: By remaining silent, the principal seemed to CONDONE bullying, GRANTing (donare) complete freedom to the bullies.
mnemonic.story_zh: 校長透過保持沉默，似乎「縱容（CONDONE）」了校園霸凌，完全給予（DONARE）了惡霸們為所欲為的自由。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = intensive prefix; connect this root idea with condone.

example: The school board made it clear that they do not condone cheating under any circumstances.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 condone 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: overlook is related, but condone has its own usage pattern and context.
pardon may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with condone.

usage_note: condone is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A change made so that someone or something can function better in a new environment, situation, or medium.
definition_zh: 適應；改編；調整

mnemonic.root_memory: APT = fit; adaptation is a change that makes something fit new conditions.
mnemonic.story_en: The novel became a film ADAPTATION after writers reshaped it to fit the screen.
mnemonic.story_zh: 作家把小說調整得適合（APT）螢幕，因此成為電影「改編（ADAPTATION）」。

example: Successful adaptation to climate change requires both new infrastructure and public planning.
example_zh: 成功適應氣候變遷需要新基礎建設與公共規劃。

near_synonyms.difference: adaptability is the ability to adapt; adaptation is the change or result.
evolution is long-term biological or social change; adaptation can be immediate or planned.

usage_note: adaptation is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: An opinion or conclusion formed on the basis of incomplete information; a guess or speculation.
definition_zh: 推測；猜測；臆測

mnemonic.story_en: Without clear data, the scientists could only THROW (jacere) random theories COM- (together) as mere CONJECTURE.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在沒有明確數據的情況下，科學家們只能把隨機的理論丟（JACERE）在一起（COM），作為一種純粹的「推測（CONJECTURE）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together; connect this root idea with conjecture.

example: The media's reporting on the celebrity's disappearance was based entirely on conjecture rather than hard facts.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 conjecture 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: speculation is related, but conjecture has its own usage pattern and context.
guesswork may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with conjecture.

usage_note: conjecture is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Standing out so as to be clearly visible; attracting notice or attention.
definition_zh: 顯眼的；引人注目的；明顯的

mnemonic.story_en: Her bright neon jacket made her highly CONSPICUOUS, forcing everyone to LOOK (specere) straight at her.
mnemonic.story_zh: 她那件明亮的霓虹夾克讓她顯得非常「引人注目（CONSPICUOUS）」，迫使每個人都盯著她看（SPECERE）。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = intensive prefix; connect this root idea with conspicuous.

example: The red warning sign was placed in a conspicuous position near the high-voltage entrance.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 conspicuous 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: noticeable is related, but conspicuous has its own usage pattern and context.
prominent may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with conspicuous.

usage_note: conspicuous is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A young person in the stage of development between childhood and adulthood.
definition_zh: 青少年；青春期的

mnemonic.root_memory: ADOLESCERE = grow up; an adolescent is someone growing toward adulthood.
mnemonic.story_en: An ADOLESCENT is still growing up, learning adult responsibilities step by step.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「青少年（ADOLESCENT）」正在長大（ADOLESCERE），一步步學習成人責任。

example: Adolescent mental health has become a major concern for schools and public health agencies.
example_zh: 青少年心理健康已成為學校與公共衛生機構的重要關切。

near_synonyms.difference: child is younger and prepubescent; adolescent refers to the teenage developmental stage.
young adult is usually older and more independent than an adolescent.

usage_note: adolescent is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: A set of equipment, tools, or organizational structures used for a particular purpose.
definition_zh: 設備；器材；機構；組織系統

mnemonic.root_memory: PARARE = prepare; an apparatus is prepared equipment for a task.
mnemonic.story_en: The laboratory APPARATUS was prepared before the experiment began.
mnemonic.story_zh: 實驗開始前，實驗「設備（APPARATUS）」已準備（PARARE）完成。

example: The researchers sterilized the apparatus before measuring the chemical reaction.
example_zh: 研究人員在測量化學反應前先將設備消毒。

near_synonyms.difference: a device is one tool; apparatus often refers to a set of tools or a system.
system is broader; apparatus often emphasizes equipment or institutional machinery.

usage_note: apparatus is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: To confirm or give support to a statement, theory, or finding with evidence or authority.
definition_zh: 證實；確證；提供證據支持

mnemonic.story_en: The witness was called to CORROBORATE the alibi, making the suspect's story look as ROBUST (strong) as an oak tree.
mnemonic.story_zh: 證人被傳喚來「證實（CORROBORATE）」不在場證明，使嫌疑人的說法看起來像橡樹一樣堅固（ROBUR）強壯。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = intensive prefix; connect this root idea with corroborate.

example: A second independent laboratory was hired to corroborate the results of the initial chemical experiment.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 corroborate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: confirm is related, but corroborate has its own usage pattern and context.
substantiate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with corroborate.

usage_note: corroborate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To postpone or delay an action or event until a later time; to submit humbly to another's wish or authority.
definition_zh: 推遲；延期；聽從；順從

mnemonic.story_en: They decided to DEFER the game, CARRYing (ferre) the schedule DE- (away) to next weekend due to rain.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由於下雨，他們決定將比賽「延期（DEFER）」，將時程表從本週末帶走（FERRE/DE）。
mnemonic.root_memory: DE- = away, down; connect this root idea with defer.

example: The student requested to defer her university admission for a year to work and gain practical experience.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 defer 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: postpone is related, but defer has its own usage pattern and context.
delay may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with defer.

usage_note: defer is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To add something to the end of a document, message, list, or file.
definition_zh: 附加；增補；加在末尾

mnemonic.root_memory: PEND = hang; append means hanging extra material onto the end.
mnemonic.story_en: The lawyer APPENDED a chart to the contract, hanging it at the end as supporting evidence.
mnemonic.story_zh: 律師把圖表掛在（PEND）合約末尾作為補充，這就是「附加（APPEND）」。

example: Please append the raw survey data to the final report for transparency.
example_zh: 請將原始調查資料附加到最終報告中以提高透明度。

near_synonyms.difference: insert means place inside; append means add at the end.
include means contain; append specifically means attach as an addition.

usage_note: append is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.

definition: Relevant and suitable for use in a particular situation, rule, or case.
definition_zh: 適用的；可應用的；相關的

mnemonic.root_memory: PLIC = fold; applicable means a rule can be folded onto a case.
mnemonic.story_en: The policy was APPLICABLE because it fit the case like a folded map over the right area.
mnemonic.story_zh: 該政策能摺合（PLIC）到這個案例上，因此是「適用的（APPLICABLE）」。

example: The discount is only applicable to students who register before the deadline.
example_zh: 此折扣只適用於截止日前註冊的學生。

near_synonyms.difference: appropriate means proper; applicable means able to be applied to a case.
valid means legally or logically sound; applicable means relevant for use.

usage_note: applicable is most natural in formal academic, legal, scientific, or professional writing when used with its common collocations.
